best_for: Amateur astronomers, teachers and stargazers who want a realistic night sky on their computer to plan an observing session or drive a telescope, at no cost.
description:
Stellarium is a planetarium for your computer, made by the Stellarium team. It shows the sky in 3D as you would see it with your own eyes, through binoculars or through a telescope.

You can switch on calendars from more than 35 cultures, the full Messier catalog of nebula images, comet tails, shooting stars and the locations of known exoplanets. It simulates eclipses, novae and supernovae, and an ocular view shows what a given eyepiece would reveal. For a planetarium dome there is fisheye projection, or spherical mirror projection for a low-cost home dome. You can add your own objects, landscapes and constellation images, and pull new solar system objects from online sources.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Stellarium is free under the GPL-2.0 license. There are no plans or paid tiers for the desktop app.

points.title: Catalogs grow on demand
points.text: The default set holds more than 600,000 stars and over 80,000 deep-sky objects. Optional catalogs add more than 220 million stars and over 1 million deep-sky objects, so you only download the depth you need.

points.title: Telescope control and scripting
points.text: It can point a telescope, run scripts and accept commands over an HTTP interface. Sky lore covers more than 40 cultures, with the Milky Way, atmosphere and sunrise drawn in 3D.

points.title: It needs a real 3D graphics card
points.text: The minimum is a 64-bit system, OpenGL 2.1 (or OpenGL ES 2.0), 1 GiB of RAM and 1 GiB of disk. The project recommends OpenGL 3.3, 4 GiB of RAM and 10 GiB of disk.

points.title: Pick the right Windows build
points.text: The Qt6 builds need Windows 10 or later and come for x64 and ARM64. The site still offers a Qt5 x64 build for Windows 7. The installers here can install for the current user or for all users.

points.title: Mac build needs macOS 11
points.text: The current universal Mac build is a Qt6 build that needs macOS 11 or later, though the general requirements list macOS 10.13 as the floor.

points.title: Linux Flatpak comes from the team
points.text: Flathub marks the Flatpak as verified, published by the Stellarium team, for x64 and ARM64. It is a large download at about 485 MB. The Windows listing keeps 47 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
